title: Claude Code Baseline Config
description: Drives which baseline hooks run and whether they block. Consumed by hooks/lib/common.sh. Resolution is purely relative - baseline.config.json points at this file with "$schema": "./baseline.config.schema.json" - so the schema deliberately carries no $id. DEGRADED-STATE CONTRACT, which no schema keyword can express: a config file that exists but does not parse is not equivalent to an absent one. Absent means 'defaults apply'; malformed means every key silently reverts to its default, so module gating reads false and commandGuard.extraPatterns vanishes. The hooks therefore test bcl_config_malformed before their enabled-gate and route that state through bcl_failclosed_exit. The 'default' keywords below document the value common.sh substitutes when a key is missing; they are annotations, not behavior - validators do not inject them.

minClaudeCodeVersion.description: Minimum Claude Code version (canonical semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, no leading zeros) the baseline's behavior was verified against. install.sh detects the live 'claude --version' and prints an advisory warning (never blocks) when it is older. Bump only alongside a RELEASING.md re-verification.

baselineVersion.description: Revision stamp for this baseline template (distinct from the schema 'version' integer). Written verbatim on a fresh install (create path only) and mirrored in hooks/VERSION; tools/baseline-status.sh --drift uses it to detect repos on an old baseline. Bump alongside hooks/VERSION every release.

enforcement.description: Global posture. 'block': hooks fail the tool call on violation. 'warn': hooks advise but never fail. Note the event asymmetry: only PreToolUse hooks can fail a tool call. A PostToolUse hook exits after the write has already happened, so under 'block' it reports the violation to Claude rather than undoing it.

failClosed.description: When a security control cannot RUN - missing or malformed rules file, malformed baseline.config.json, or Python unavailable - fail closed: under 'block' posture the hook exits 2 with a loud message instead of silently passing. Defaults to true, and the default is what a hook gets when this file is unreadable, so the degraded path is fail-closed by construction. Set false to downgrade such degradations to warnings. It does not cover a hook that never launches (deleted or non-executable script): Claude Code's exit-code semantics make that a fail-open no hook can intercept.

guardrails.description: Guardrails that only INSPECT are on unless disabled, so an absent config never means absent enforcement. autoFormat is the exception - it executes code and is opt-in. Disable an inspecting guardrail only with deliberate intent.

commandGuard.description: PreToolUse inspection of proposed shell commands (matcher Bash|PowerShell). Inspects only; executes nothing from the repo, so it is on by default.

extraPatterns.description: Additional case-insensitive substrings that block a shell command (Bash or PowerShell). Silently dropped if this file does not parse, which is why the hooks fail closed on a malformed config.

autoFormat.description: Runs the repo's formatters after a write. DEFAULT FALSE, and the only guardrail that executes repo-supplied code: ./node_modules/.bin/prettier and ./node_modules/.bin/eslint are the target repository's own binaries, their config files (prettier.config.js, eslint.config.js) and plugins are repo-controlled, and 'dotnet format' builds the project. Enable it only for a repo whose toolchain you trust. The hook reads this key with bcl_guardrail_opted_in, so only a literal true in a readable config enables it - a missing key, a missing config or an unreadable one keeps it off.

modules.description: Opt-in hooks. Off by default; enable per repo. 'Off by default' is also the fallback when this file cannot be read, so a corrupted config never silently enables a module - but it does silently DISABLE the ones you enabled, which is why the hooks fail closed on a malformed config instead of treating it as absent.

rulesFile.description: Path (repo-relative or absolute) to the declarative rules file.

requireWhenEnv.description: If non-empty, only enforce when this environment variable is set.

configGuard.description: ConfigChange tamper-detection. When enabled, watches in-session changes to the settings files the baseline wires it to - .claude/settings.json (source project_settings) and .claude/settings.local.json (source local_settings, which overrides it) - and blocks/warns if the baseline hook wiring or deny-list is stripped, or disableAllHooks is set. Detection after the fact, in-session only: it sees a change Claude Code reports, not an edit made while no session is running, and it does not watch baseline.config.json or the hook scripts themselves.

commitGrep.description: Literal substring matched against recent commit subjects (fixed-string, not a regex).
